subject.title: fix(chat): preserve PNG attachments in native clients

question: Should native clients preserve every PNG input, preserve PNG only when alpha is present, or retain the existing always-JPEG normalization policy?
rationale: The current JPEG behavior and alpha flattening were intentional and tested, while this PR changes the user-visible transport contract across three native surfaces; code review cannot choose the permanent format and bandwidth tradeoff without product intent.

options.title: Preserve alpha PNGs
options.body: Keep transparent PNGs as bounded PNG output while converting opaque images to bounded JPEG, matching the existing documented image-policy precedent and minimizing payload growth.

options.title: Preserve every PNG
options.body: Accept the PR's broader format-preservation contract after adding real native proof for opaque and transparent PNGs, metadata stripping, and payload limits.

options.title: Retain JPEG normalization
options.body: Keep the existing native transport policy and close the PR if preserving transparency is not worth the additional format and payload surface.

recommendation.title: Preserve alpha PNGs
recommendation.body: Keep transparent PNGs as bounded PNG output while converting opaque images to bounded JPEG, matching the existing documented image-policy precedent and minimizing payload growth.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and tested the current Apple attachment policy, making them the strongest available feature-history routing candidate, though final product authority may sit elsewhere.
